newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, interest thin.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, interest thin.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late trading on Friday, with buying interest remaining thin despite gains in Malaysia, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,410-15 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening. Crude palm oil was on offer at around 1,200 rupiah/kg in Sumatra's Medan.

"The market was drifting, with not much action although Malaysian prices were on the rise after some good export numbers," one trader said. "This past week, movements in Malaysia seem to have little impact on Indonesian prices."
Traders said they expected prices to remain weak next week on continued poor demand and ample supply. "There's plenty of oil in the market in Jakarta, and buyers can afford to wait."
They said exports would be boosted by the Indonesian currency's decline against the U.S. dollar and that this could lead to lower prices in Europe.
"Export prices are still good because of the weak rupiah," one trader said. "Increased exports, however, could lead to lower palm olein and crude palm prices in Europe."

August crude palm oil offers were quoted at $475 a tonne CIF Rotterdam on Thursday, down $2.50, while September was quoted at $482.50, down $2.50. August palm olein was quoted unchanged at $520, and September was also unchanged at $515.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Normar Splendor will leave for India on Saturday with 6,000 tonnes of palm oil, while the MT Grazla will leave for Dumai on Sunday with 12,000 tonnes of palm kernel oil.
